Held-out EBs flagged as candidates: detached or not agrees with Morph < 0.5, 95% interval lower bound >= 0.60
Seven planet hosts and quiet stars: at most one flagged as an eclipsing-binary candidate
Synthetic detached EBs injected into the seven contrast light curves: period within 0.5%, 95% interval lower bound >= 0.85
Held-out Canto Martins et al. (2020) stars: a rotation period detected, 95% interval lower bound >= 0.70
Held-out stars: period within 10% of the published one (an undetected star is a miss), 95% interval lower bound >= 0.60
Held-out stars: within 10% of the published period, half or double it, 95% interval lower bound >= 0.75
Held-out matches: |ours - published| within twice the combined uncertainty for at least 68%
Three quiet stars (pi Men, zeta Tuc, beta Hyi, sector 1): no rotation period detected
Synthetic spot modulation (1-12 d, 1-20 ppt) injected into the three quiet stars: period within 10%, 95% interval lower bound >= 0.85
Held-out Fausnaugh et al. (2023) type Ia supernovae: a transient candidate within 10 d of their peak, 95% interval lower bound >= 0.60

Detected held-out supernovae: rise time ours/theirs, bootstrap 95% interval of the median inside [0.67, 1.5]
Detected held-out supernovae: peak TESS magnitude ours minus theirs, bootstrap 95% interval of the median inside [-0.5, +0.5] mag
Detected held-out supernovae: class hint extragalactic-transient-like, 95% interval lower bound >= 0.60
Proxima Cen S11-12: transient candidates matching a Medina et al. (2020) flare, class hint flare-like, 95% interval lower bound >= 0.80
Three quiet stars, sector 1: fewer than 0.05 transient candidates per day not marked as likely false alarms
Control apertures beside the held-out supernovae: at most 10% carry an extragalactic-transient-like candidate
Synthetic momentum-dump spikes and asteroid-like bumps injected into the quiet stars: marked as likely false alarms, 95% interval lower bound >= 0.80

unvalidated: Planet vetting: unchanged. The eclipsing-binary module's vetting hints are advisory, no vetting decision uses them, and they were not evaluated; using them in vetting needs its own pre-registered evaluation.

Eclipse widths: Prša et al. (2022) give 2-Gaussian widths, SetuHQ a full width at half depth, so only their rank order is compared. The e·cosω values are first-order hints from the secondary's phase, not compared with radial-velocity orbits.

Rotation: one sector per star, as the protocol fixes; periods longer than about 13 days are not measured, and stitching sectors (with care for sector-to-sector offsets) is not done and not validated. Canto Martins et al. (2020) used every sector available to them.

Transients: one TESScut sector per supernova, as the protocol fixes. When first light falls before that sector begins, the reference image already holds supernova light, so the rise time and the peak brightness are measured from a non-zero floor; the supernovae compared are all type Ia, so the extragalactic class hint is not tested on tidal disruption events or other transients.

Scattered light: no labelled real sample was found; the screen (quality flags and control apertures) is described and exercised on synthetic events and the supernova cutouts' control apertures, not validated against a catalogue of scattered-light events.

Asteroid crossings: screened by shape and, in cutouts, by a moving centroid; no catalogue of TESS asteroid crossings was compared (Fausnaugh et al. 2023's asteroid flags excluded those supernovae from the sample).

references.binaries: Prša et al. 2022, ApJS 258, 16 (TESS Eclipsing Binary stars I, sectors 1-26), VizieR J/ApJS/258/16; the 2-Gaussian model columns (Dp-2g, Wp-2g, Phip-2g, Ds-2g, Ws-2g, Phis-2g), the period and the morphology coefficient (Matijevič et al. 2012: 0 widest detached, 1 ellipsoidal)
references.rotation: Canto Martins et al. 2020, ApJS 250, 20 (rotation periods of TESS objects of interest), VizieR J/ApJS/250/20, table 1 (unambiguous rotation periods)
references.transients: Fausnaugh et al. 2023, ApJ 956, 108 (four years of type Ia supernovae observed by TESS), VizieR J/ApJ/956/108, table 1 (peak TESS magnitude, time of peak) and table 3 (time of first light, rise time). Table 3's BJD column is BJD - 2457000 (the ReadMe says 2470000; the values are in the TESS range).

labels: An eclipsing binary or a transient SetuHQ finds is a candidate, never new and never confirmed.
Morphology and transient classes are heuristic hints from the light curve alone.
